thread:
alex: quick brain dump \u2014 i'm prototyping a prewarm handshake for the api gateway. idea: client marks intent, gateway returns a short-lived lease (103 or 202) while it primes upstream conns / node-local caches, then client references lease on the real request. thoughts?
dina: interesting. main win is reducing tail for short read paths. two immediate design q's: 1) how do we guarantee prewarm doesn't execute side effects, 2) how do retries/hedging interact?
raj: agree. my suggestion: prewarm requests MUST be safe-only by default (GET/HEAD). if a route allows non-safe methods, require an explicit idempotency token or an allowlist flag in platform config.
zoe: handshake sketch: client -> gateway with header `x-rw-prefetch: intent`. gateway responds `103 Prefetch-Lease: id=lk9f; ttl=400` and starts warm. when client sends actual request it includes `x-rw-lease: lk9f`. upstream sees `x-rw-prefetch-lease` and can decide to materialize warmed state. no automatic commits.
alex: nice. what about streaming (chunked) endpoints? we want partial response warmups too. maybe send initial metadata with `prefetch-status: ok|miss|inflight` and final trailer `prefetch-trailer: cost_ms=..;state=applied|ignored`.
dina: also need quota and abuse protection. prewarm could be amplified (client spams intents). propose tenant-level token bucket + per-route max concurrency. keep default conservative.
raj: billing: treat prewarm as non-billable on hosted for now and surface as opt-in for Dedicated. otherwise customers will get surprised. also emit metrics: prefetch_requests, prefetch_accept_rate, prefetch_hit_latency_reduction.
zoe: hedging: if client hedges (sends two concurrent requests) and both ask for prewarm, we need deterministic binding. simplest: lease ownership semantics  first successful lease binds the warmed state; others get `prefetch-status: joined` or `ignored`. leave tie-breaking deterministic by lease timestamp.
alex: failure modes: if prewarm fails, we shouldn't cause request failures. prewarm must be a hint only. gateway should fall back to normal request path if warm misses or errors. return prefetch-status: miss and continue.
dina: implementation note: avoid duplicating K/V cache in the edge. prefer warming upstream node-local caches or warming shared cache with expiry tags. otherwise frontend memory explodes. track per-node memory delta during prewarm.
raj: security: ensure prewarm header can't be forged between internal services. validate via mTLS or internal ACLs. also strip prewarm headers for external traffic that isn't allowed.
zoe: proto example headers: `x-rw-prefetch: 1
x-rw-prefetch-mode: conn,kv
x-rw-lease-ttl-ms: 400
x-rw-prefetch-safety: safe`
alex: config sample: `ingress.prefetch: enabled: true; default_ttl_ms: 400; routes: [ {prefix: /v1/fast, methods: [GET]} ]; max_concurrent_per_tenant: 4`
infra-bot: canary report: prewarm-canary v1 rolled to 15% traffic for /v1/fast. metrics: cold p95 down 120ms, upstream conns +11% during lease windows, prefetch_rejects 2.3% (quota).
dina: action items: alex to draft compact RFC w/ handshake wire format + header list, zoe to write hedging semantics, raj to draft safety/idempotency rules + billing note. i'll coordinate canary runway.
alex: i'll open RFC: "gateway prefetch lease handshake" and include header samples + example streaming trailer. target: RFC up by Fri.
infra-bot: RFC created: https://rfc.internal/r/2090-gateway-prefetch-lease-handshake
alex: thanks, moving to RFC review.
